task_name: the process runner port, the border, and the tool runner behind it
summary: ProcessRunner (backend/src/infrastructure/process-runner.ts) is a new must-implement port with runAndWait/launch and the structural LaunchedProcess type; SystemProcesses (process-border.ts) implements it over node:child_process's execFile/spawn and reads no `this`. ToolRunner now takes a required `processes: ProcessRunner` and delegates run()/#spawned() to it instead of importing node:child_process itself; ct-api.ts builds exactly one SystemProcesses (CtApi.#PROCESSES) and injects it into all seven ToolRunner construction sites. The census's SPAWNING regex needed a more careful design than a bare `launch|runAndWait` addition: `launch` already names an unrelated PlanAgents/ExternalTool concept in ~7 files under backend/src (start-plan.ts, start-milestone-plan.ts, plan-agents.ts, run-plan-agents.ts, headless-plan-agents.ts, ct-groom-epic.ts, external-tool.ts), so a bare identifier match would have wrongly flagged all of them as unaccounted process spawns. I scoped the new alternatives to (a) calls literally qualified by a `processes.` receiver, and (b) declarations of `launch(binary:`/`runAndWait(binary:`/`openTerminal(file:` — matching only this port's own contracted signatures — verified this produces zero false positives across backend/src and exactly the intended matches in tool-runner.ts, process-runner.ts and process-border.ts. ACCOUNTED gained process-border.ts (reason: THE_BORDER) and process-runner.ts (reason: DECLARES_ONLY) verbatim as the brief specified, and tool-runner.ts's row now lists ['launch','runAndWait']. Every test/fixture across the backend that constructed a bare `new ToolRunner(...)` was updated to inject a `SystemProcesses` instance (real process construction, so all *-real-process tests still launch real children exactly as before). Verification run: `npm run typecheck` (exit 0), the three task verification commands (exit 0), plus the full backend suite (`env -u CT_STATE_DIR npx vitest run`): 153 files / 3217 tests passed, and `git status --porcelain -- plugin frontend` is empty. No plan amendment was needed; all touched paths were already inside Task 1's Files: line.

the process table port, and every kill, liveness read and terminal behind it
summary:
Added ProcessTable (backend/src/infrastructure/process-table.ts: TerminalOptions, TableRead, Terminal, ProcessTable throw-stub, TerminalSpawn). SystemProcesses in process-border.ts now also implements ProcessTable: signal() wraps process.kill, readTable() is the real bounded /bin/ps execFile read (moved byte-for-byte out of PtyLiveSessions.#inspectProcessTable, bounded by the TableRead argument instead of the class constants), openTerminal() wraps node-pty's spawn (aliased to ptySpawn to avoid colliding with node:child_process's spawn already imported for launch()). PtyLiveSessions lost its built-in default inspector and the execFile/node:child_process import entirely; inspectProcessTable is now a required ProcessTable['readTable'], and Terminal/TerminalSpawn are re-exported from process-table.ts instead of being declared locally. ToolRunner gained a required signal: ProcessTable['signal'] field and uses it instead of a bare process.kill(-processGroup, 'SIGTERM') in its onSpawn-abandonment cleanup. CheckedRunDelivery's optional alive port is gone; it now takes a required signal: ProcessTable['signal'] and its #alive check calls this.signal(pid, 0) instead of process.kill directly. ct-api.ts no longer imports node-pty or uses process.kill for the live-session wiring: PtyLiveSessions' spawn/signal/inspectProcessTable are all bound to the existing CtApi.#PROCESSES SystemProcesses instance, and every ToolRunner/CheckedRunDelivery construction site (7 ToolRunner + 1 CheckedRunDelivery in ct-api.ts) now passes signal from that same instance. spawned-children.ts's ACCOUNTED table gained an entry for process-table.ts (openTerminal declaration site) and process-border.ts's entry now lists execFile twice (runAndWait's and readTable's own execFile calls) plus openTerminal; pty-live-sessions.ts's entry dropped execFile (moved out) and keeps only spawn. Added the owed test 'the_process_table_read_carries_the_inspection_bounds' in pty-live-sessions.test.ts and hand-verified it goes red when the call site's timeoutMs is perturbed.

The ripple from making ToolRunner.signal, CheckedRunDelivery.signal and PtyLiveSessions.inspectProcessTable required (per D-6/D-7, since every process.kill and the /bin/ps read must live in the border) reached well beyond the five production files the brief named: tool-runner-real-process.test.ts, tool-runner-whole-output-real-process.test.ts, git-workspace-real-process.test.ts, claude-conversations.test.ts, claude-conversations-real-process.test.ts, session-channel-real-process.test.ts and fixtures/{delivery-publisher.ts,run-driver-mother.ts} all had to gain a signal field or fix their Terminal/TerminalSpawn import path, purely mechanically (each already held a SystemProcesses instance under some name and now also passes its .signal). I read all of them as within 'the tests that build these classes' rather than amending Files, since each literally constructs ToolRunner, CheckedRunDelivery or PtyLiveSessions.

The four 'the default inspector ...' tests in pty-live-sessions.test.ts used to exercise PtyLiveSessions' own built-in /bin/ps reader with node:child_process mocked. Since that reader moved to SystemProcesses.readTable and the brief's Tests line says nothing is removed on purpose, I kept them by wiring inspectProcessTable to a real SystemProcesses instance (with node:child_process still mocked in the same file), rather than deleting them or spinning up a separate process-border test file the Files line never authorized.

Verified: cd backend && npm run typecheck (exit 0); the three brief verification commands all pass; the full backend suite (153 files, 3221 tests) is green under env -u CT_STATE_DIR npx vitest run.

the headless worker and the claude calls launch through the border
summary: The TDD skill loaded cleanly. headless-call-worker.ts and claude-calls.ts now type spawn as ProcessRunner['launch'] and kill as ProcessTable['signal'], with LaunchedProcess replacing ChildProcess, and main() builds a SystemProcesses and passes processes.launch/processes.signal instead of importing node:child_process directly. ct-api.ts drops its spawnChild import and wires ClaudeCalls with CtApi.#PROCESSES.launch; spawned-children.ts drops the now-unused ct-api.ts ACCOUNTED row and the INJECTS_ONLY constant, since ct-api.ts no longer imports a spawning library. The new census test passes and I additionally verified it fails for the right reason against the pre-task source (importersUnder returns 4 files, not just the border) using an isolated scratch copy, since the test was added close in sequence to the source edits rather than strictly before them. grep -rlE over backend/src now returns only process-border.ts. Beyond the three named files, every test under backend/__tests__ that constructs ClaudeCalls or HeadlessCallWorker directly needed its spawn/kill typing updated to compile against the new port types: fixtures/run-driver-mother.ts gained a small launch() adapter on its FixtureProcesses fixture (mirroring SystemProcesses.launch) because its own spawn field still serves callers that need Node's native options shape (e.g. hold()'s string stdio); claude-calls-real-process.test.ts now spawns through a real SystemProcesses().launch instead of the bare node:child_process spawn, matching how production now launches; the remaining files only needed their `as typeof import('node:child_process').spawn` casts retargeted to `ProcessRunner['launch']`, or a bare unused real spawn reference (in never-invoked recovery/observation doubles) replaced by a directly-typed throwing stub. npm run typecheck is clean, the whole backend suite passes (3222/3222; one pty-live-sessions-real-process flake under full-suite parallel load reproduced green in isolation and on a full rerun, and touches no file from this task). No plan amendment was needed: no path outside backend/src/infrastructure/{headless-call-worker,claude-calls,ct-api}.ts, backend/__tests__/spawned-children.{ts,test.ts}, and 'the tests that build ClaudeCalls or HeadlessCallWorker' was touched, and plugin/ and frontend/ are untouched.
